messages.content: Predict one actual allocation in the Independence Dilemma, an online group decision task with6members. There are10rounds. At the start of EVERY round each person receives10fresh monetary units(MU);earlier kept money is accumulated earnings,not an extra current endowment. Each simultaneously allocates the10MU among a public pool shared by the group,a separate private pool belonging only to that person,and money kept for themselves. Each component can be0through10MU and all three must sum to10. Investments accumulate in their respective pools across rounds. The public threshold is240MU for the group;the private threshold is60MU for the individual. At the end of round10,if the shared public pool reaches at least240MU,EVERY group member keeps all money they held back over the rounds,irrespective of their personal contribution. If public success fails but the person’s own private pool reaches at least60MU,only that person keeps their held-back money. Either threshold is sufficient. If neither threshold is reached,the person loses all held-back money. Money invested into either pool is not refunded or separately paid. The rate disclosed at the beginning of this stage is10MU=USD1. The number of rounds and both thresholds are known. Every round gives a new allocation opportunity,including after a threshold has been reached. Current other-member allocations and current cumulative outcomes are not known before the simultaneous choice. After each completed round,the feedback schedule provides own private accumulated investment,the shared public accumulated investment,and other group members’ allocations. All locally recoverable prior-round allocations and totals are supplied below. The log does not record receipt of individual feedback screens. Other members’ allocations are supplied as an unordered list within each round;their displayed identities across rounds are not established by the available materials. The list order does not identify a member. This task follows a binary trust-game stage with2trial rounds and15main rounds. Fixed randomly assigned roles are Truster or Trustee;partners change each round,and the exact session size was not disclosed during the trust game. The Truster can keep an endowment or send it;following a send,the Trustee can keep or return. The assigned trust-game terminal payoffs below are ordered(Truster,Trustee)in experimental points. Use these endpoint payoffs without assuming a conserved transfer formula. At the end of each trust-game round,session percentages of trust/reciprocity are reported,with no other players’ individual histories. The participant’s trust-game experience,these earlier feedback values,and the actual own total dollars displayed at the end of that stage cannot be recovered from the available record. Those values are unavailable in this prediction record;this does not mean the participant did not know or experience them. The trust-game point conversion rate was not announced beforehand. The age supplied was measured in the final survey and is used only as stable self-known background. Later attitude/trust/political/risk ratings are not prior features. Predict the observed whole-MU joint allocation. Output only a JSON object in this fixed field order:{"public_MU":integer,"private_MU":integer,"kept_MU":integer};each0through10,total10. The source reports whole MU;finer UI precision is not documented.
